subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit an existing policy layer such as `tools.subagents.tools`, or rely on per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested config, and choosing precedence/default behavior changes a security and compatibility surface for unattended jobs.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against global/provider/agent/sandbox/subagent policy and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as inheriting `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing new config but coupling two different session types.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Do not add a global cron policy and instead document/configure per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against global/provider/agent/sandbox/subagent policy and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from cron tool-policy and delivery history plus prior review context for this issue.
